 Tamil song based on Bharathiyar poem makes Grammy history
 Composed and sung by Devan Ekambaram, the track interprets a devotional poem by Tamil poet and freedom fighter Subramania Bharati.
 Harsh Tiwari 
 17 November, 2026 02:50 pm IST

 New Delhi: Tamil music has made history at the Grammy Awards. Varuvaaiy, composed and sung by Devan Ekambaram, featuring vocalist Subhiksha Rangarajan, has become the first Tamil song to earn a Grammy nomination. The song has been nominated in the Best Global Music Performance category at the 69th Grammy Awards, scheduled to take place in February 2027.
 The nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards were announced on November 16 and Varuvaaiy remains India’s only nomination in the category this year.
 “I’m so thrilled, proud and honoured to share that VARUVAAIY has been nominated in the Best Global Music Performance category for the 69th Grammy Awards. Not only for me and Susha, but this is such a special moment because it’s the very 1st Tamil Song to ever be nominated and am so happy it’s a BHARATHIAR song,” Ekambaram wrote on his Instagram
 Show Full Article
 The singer composer also reflected on his journey as an independent Tamil musician, which began in 1998. He made his playback singing debut with AR Rahman’s 1999 film Kadhalar Dhinam , lending his voice to the popular song Oh Maria. He has sung in more than 500 film soundtracks across Tamil and other South Indian languages.
 “Though most of you know me as a singer, the composer and producer in me has been longing for years and years for a moment like this,” he wrote, adding that November 16 would remain an unforgettable day for him.
 Also read: ‘Love Pattinson, hate this choice’—fans react to new James Bond casting 
 A devotional poem  
 Varuvaaiy is an interpretation of a devotional poem by renowned Tamil poet and freedom fighter Subramania Bharati. Dedicated to Lord Krishna, the poem invokes the deity to enter human consciousness and destroy evil.
 Vocalist Subhiksha Rangarajan, who features in the song, trained in Carnatic classical music before pursuing jazz studies at the University of Toronto.
 At the Grammys, Varuvaaiy will compete against tracks by Angélique Kidjo featuring Pharrell Williams and Quavo, Rosalía and Dougie F, Shakira and Burna Boy, and KerreKe, Mireya Ramos and Alex E Chávez.
